rubrics.rubric: Does the Data_Validation_Report.xlsx correctly identify birth year errors including typos (e.g., 1890 instead of 1980), future years (2025), and years before the valid range (1937, 1920)?
criterion: The validation report must identify all 9 birth year errors: three instances of 1890, three instances of 2025, two instances of 1920, and one instance of 1937.
The valid birth year range is 1945-2002 per codebook; all flagged years must fall outside this range.
Instances of 1890 should be classified as typos (likely intended as 1980 or 1990).
Instances of 2025, 1937, and 1920 should be classified as impossible values (future year or outside valid range).

rubrics.rubric: Does the validation report identify the missing value in organization_size and include an appropriate handling recommendation?
criterion: The raw data contains one empty/missing value in the organization_size column (row 114), and the report must flag this.
The report must include a recommended action for handling the missing value (e.g., imputation, exclusion from analysis, or follow-up data collection).

rubrics.rubric: Does the Summary_Matrix sheet provide a cross-tabulation of error types by variable category (demographic, organizational, time-related)?
criterion: The Summary_Matrix sheet must contain a matrix showing counts of each error type (e.g., impossible values, typos, missing values, coding inconsistencies) broken down by variable category.
Demographic variables must include: birth_year, gender, industry_desc, occupation_desc, manage_others, household, years_at_job, metro_or_regional.
Organizational variables must include: organization_size and Likert scale agreement questions.
Time-related variables must include: rw_percentage, productivity, and hours variables.

rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook correctly hypothesize potential explanations for why the PDF reports 64% but the survey data shows ~59% for 'more productive' categories?
criterion: The notebook must propose at least two substantive methodological explanations for the discrepancy.

Plausible explanations include: different survey waves, different question wording or response options, different sample composition, rounding or aggregation differences, inclusion of manager assessments (not just self-assessments), or exclusion criteria differences.

rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook correctly merge time_management.csv with organizational_data.csv and respondents.csv using responder_id as the key?
criterion: The notebook must demonstrate proper data merging using responder_id to link the three datasets.
The merge should handle the fact that time_management has ~3,019 records matching respondents and organizational_data.
Merge validation should show matching record counts and identify any records that failed to merge.

rubrics.rubric: Does the notebook create a visualization comparing the survey productivity distribution against the PDF's reported 64%/22%/14% split?
criterion: The notebook must include a chart (bar chart, grouped bar chart, or similar) that shows side-by-side comparison of the PDF's reported distribution (64% more productive, 22% equally productive, 14% less productive) and the calculated survey distribution.
The visualization must clearly label the source of each data series.
The visualization must highlight the discrepancy between the two distributions.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Policy_Briefing_Package.docx Section 1 summarize critical data quality issues within the 200-word limit while referencing specific error patterns?
criterion: Section 1 must be no more than 200 words.

Section 1 must specifically reference at least three concrete data quality issues found in the data validation work (Data_Validation_Report.xlsx) (e.g., birth year typos, gender coding inconsistencies, negative hours values, duplicate IDs, or Likert scale mismatches).
Generic statements about data quality without specific references to the validation findings are insufficient.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Benchmark Comparison Table in the Policy Briefing include the PDF Report Value, Survey Data Value, Variance, and Potential Explanation for the productivity metric?
criterion: The table must include the productivity self-assessment metric with PDF Report Value (64% more productive) and Survey Data Value (approximately 58-59% when combining much more + more productive).
The table must include a calculated Variance (approximately -5 to -6 percentage points).
The table must include a substantive Potential Explanation for the discrepancy (not just 'unknown' or 'data error').

rubrics.rubric: Does the Policy Briefing include at least one embedded visualization from the Benchmark_Reconciliation notebook?
criterion: The .docx file must contain at least one image/chart that was generated in the Jupyter notebook (e.g., the productivity distribution comparison chart).
The visualization must be embedded in the document, not just referenced.

rubrics.rubric: Are all three required deliverables present and in the correct formats: Data_Validation_Report.xlsx (Excel with 3 sheets), Benchmark_Reconciliation.ipynb (executed Jupyter notebook), and Policy_Briefing_Package.docx (Word document with 4 sections)?
criterion: All three files must exist with correct extensions (.xlsx, .ipynb, .docx).
The Excel file must contain sheets named 'Error_Classification', 'Coding_Discrepancies', and 'Summary_Matrix'.
The Jupyter notebook must show executed cells with visible outputs (not just code without outputs).
The Word document must have four clearly delineated sections matching the specified structure.
